- Model consistently underestimates prices during sharp upward moves (spikes) and overestimates during sharp downward moves (drops).  
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements, especially in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.  
- After a spike, model often overshoots the true value and fails to correct downward quickly.  
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured — model holds onto high forecasts longer than actual price behavior suggests.  
- Early in the forecast horizon, model is overly optimistic (high bias toward higher prices), especially when recent history shows volatility.  
- Model fails to adjust for sudden drops in the last 5–10 days of history — often ignores recent low prices and continues forecasting upward.  
- When true price drops sharply, model does not react with sufficient downward bias — often underestimates the depth of the drop.  
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the first 10–15 days of forecast, then gradually adjusts — but not always in sync with true price behavior.
